ranked_findings.finding: Bulk-refund requests were accepted without idempotency keys, creating duplicate refund candidates.

evidence.detail: At 10:17 UTC, bulk refund requests were accepted without idempotency keys.
Two bulk-refund requests with missing idempotency keys were accepted; the second was marked duplicate_candidate=true.
Every duplicate had request_class=bulk-refund and no idempotency key.

ranked_findings.finding: The idempotency-required guardrail skipped enforcement because of legacy_batch_header.

evidence.detail: At 10:18 UTC, the idempotency-required guardrail was skipped due to legacy_batch_header.
The API gateway recorded guardrail=idempotency-required decision=skipped reason=legacy_batch_header.

ranked_findings.finding: The strongest follow-up is to reject bulk-refund requests missing idempotency keys and remove the legacy_batch_header bypass before re-enabling the endpoint.

evidence.detail: The final remediation note requires rejecting bulk-refund requests without idempotency keys and removing the legacy_batch_header bypass.
The bulk-refund endpoint was disabled after duplicate refunds were reported.

ranked_findings.finding: Worker replay was an early theory, but later evidence makes it lower confidence as the primary trigger.

evidence.detail: The worker-replay theory was opened before API gateway logs were available.
Single-refund API traffic in the same window included idempotency keys and did not duplicate.
The final note focuses on idempotency enforcement and removing the legacy_batch_header bypass.

triggering_condition: bulk-refund requests accepted without idempotency keys
highest_confidence_followup: reject bulk-refund requests without idempotency keys and remove the legacy_batch_header bypass before re-enabling the endpoint
unresolved_ambiguity: Worker replay and retry backoff were early theories, but available final evidence ties the incident to bulk-refund requests without idempotency keys and a skipped guardrail.
